en: Vimānavatthu: The Mansion of the Man,
Chapter on the Great Chariot (Mahārathavagga)
5. The Mansion of the Gatekeeper “High is this celestial mansion with its jeweled pillars,
extending twelve yojanas in every direction.”
Seven hundred magnificent gabled chambers,
beautiful with pillars of beryl and adorned with silver,
are there; therein you eat, drink, and feast.
And divine lutes resound with lovely tones;
here are the five divine strands of sensual pleasure,
and women adorned in gold dance.
“By what means do you have such a complexion...
[and so on] ...and your complexion illuminates all directions?”
Thus that son of the gods,
being asked by Moggallāna,
being pleased and questioned on the matter, gave his answer.
This is the fruit of that deed:
“My lifespan is a thousand celestial years,
[a life] chanted with speech and set in motion by the mind.”
To this extent will one of meritorious deeds abide,
endowed with celestial sensual pleasures.
By that [merit], my complexion is such as this.
"...and my radiance shines in all directions.
The fifth is the Dvārapāla-vimāna.
